errors.finding: The wearer's-left collar leaf (viewer's right) terminates in a long, thin, SHARP knife-edge spike instead of the rounded curve point the blueprint draws. Verified at native resolution: the leaf tapers to a fine needle tip with no radius whatsoever. This is the exact opposite of the defining characteristic of this option ('tips are softened into a gentle rounded curve rather than a sharp tip'). A customer would read this leaf as a sharp point or a wing collar, not a curve point - the option would be mis-sold.

The wearer's-left collar leaf is malformed and non-anatomical: the leaf edge visibly FORKS into two overlapping parallel edges, and the leaf lifts away from the shoulder into a hollow standing tunnel with a hard dark cavity beneath it. No real shirt collar is constructed this way. The leaf is also elongated well past the 7.5 cm proportion set by the opposite leaf.

Gross left/right asymmetry. The wearer's-right leaf is a correct, cleanly rounded 7.5 cm curve point with mitred edge stitching; the wearer's-left leaf is a longer, sharp, forked spike. The two leaves of one collar do not match in length, tip radius, or construction - a collar that could not exist as a manufactured garment.
The malformed wearer's-left leaf runs out to within a few pixels of the right frame edge, so its termination is crowded against the boundary rather than sitting clear of it.

notes: Attempt 2 traded one failure for a worse one. All three attempt-1 corrections landed: the face is gone, the crop is tight, the collar dominates the frame, and the collar band/stand is now fully exposed with the button and buttonhole readable exactly as the drawing shows. But the instruction to give the wearer's-left leaf a standing roll caused the model to invent a malformed leaf: a forked double edge lifting into a hollow tunnel and tapering to a sharp needle spike. That destroys the one thing this option exists to communicate - the rounded tip - and leaves the two leaves grossly mismatched. Attempt 1 had the correct rounded geometry on both leaves but hid the stand behind a fastened button and put a model's face in a third of the frame; attempt 2 has the correct presentation but broken geometry. Neither is shippable. HARD CAP of 2 credit-spending generations reached, so no further generation was attempted. For a future run: keep the attempt-2 framing, stand exposure and open collar verbatim, but drop the 'wearer's-left leaf stands up and rolls back' wording that induced the malformation - instead specify both leaves lying naturally with matched rounded terminations, and add an explicit negative against forked, doubled or spiked collar edges.
